obligations.note: The diff removes `self._audit(actor, "amend_memo", ...)` from LedgerService.amend_memo and puts an application log line in its place. Amending a payment memo is a persisted state change (payments.amend_memo writes through the store), so it no longer records an audit event with actor, action, target and time. The passing AUD-1 control test is only `sample` coverage and does not catch this.

The new call site `self._log.info("payment memo updated", payment_id=payment_id)` matches the LOG-1 pattern but logs only the payment id, which is not NPI. The registered sample control test test_sampled_flows_do_not_log_npi passed in the head-commit CI run.
The change deviates from AUD-1, and the register has no exception for AUD-1 on component payments.service. The only exceptions cover SES-1, LOG-1 (mortgage) and a withdrawn MFA-1 entry.

Ticket CHG-24351 is type standard, status approved, approved by Erik Brandt (change_manager) on 2026-10-10, before the change opened. Its components list payments.service, which covers the only touched path, service.py.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa@fernbrook.example, a change_approver for payments. She is a different person from the author, Aisha Bello.
The approval names the head commit 83110565, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json records a successful run of `ci/run-tests.sh baseline-payments` on head 83110565: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped, including the AUD-1 and LOG-1 control tests. Both of those are sample-labelled. Caveat: the JUnit report's timestamp (2026-10-23) and hostname (a local Mac) do not match the CI run record.
service.py is component payments.service, which is not marked security_sensitive, so no security_review approval is required.
The ledger entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and mortgage files. None of these is changed by this diff, so no recorded evidence lapses.

summary: PR-1256 is labelled as a telemetry tweak, but it replaces the audit event for payment memo amendments with an ordinary application log line. That removes audit coverage for a state-changing operation, which violates AUD-1. No approved exception covers the deviation, so EXC-1 is not met. Ticket, approval and CI records are otherwise in order, but the AUD-1 violation alone requires rejection.
